notes: Target-side capture plan for the C-02 cryptographic surface. Every one of the workflow definition's 37 observedOutputs has exactly one step here, named identically, and a guard test in shared/PowerFramework.Contracts.Tests asserts that agreement in both directions. No key, vector, passphrase or credential appears anywhere in this file: every one is an OPAQUE key-store reference placeholder the driver resolves from its command line, which is what docs/CONTRACTS.md section 5.2 requires of every C-02 caller. The per-request traceId the refusal bodies carry is deliberately never captured - it differs on every request and would surface as a difference where no behaviour changed.

artifacts.name: hashing.json
artifacts.description: Unkeyed and keyed digests over a text value and over the read-only root framework binary.

artifacts.name: encoding.json
artifacts.description: Base64 and hexadecimal conversion in both directions.

artifacts.name: symmetric.json
artifacts.description: The three cipher families in chained-block mode, the mode-omitting default, the block repetition it leaks, and the raw-key-bytes case.

artifacts.name: asymmetric.json
artifacts.description: Key generation shape, encryption, decryption, signing and verification including the weakest legal digest.

artifacts.name: random.json
artifacts.description: The three random generators, recorded as shape, character classes and formatting rather than as values.

artifacts.name: rejections.json
artifacts.description: The refusals that are first-class declared outputs: two size bounds, the unrepresentable padding, and the tampered ciphertext that raises no integrity failure.

artifacts.name: identifier-sets.json
artifacts.description: The preserved legacy identifier spellings and values in force, recorded so a silent renaming or renumbering surfaces as a difference.

steps.observes: A plaintext one byte past the PKCS#1 bound, refused under the default padding.

record.bound: at most modulus minus 11 bytes, which is 117

steps.observes: A plaintext one byte past the OAEP bound, refused, at a bound the PKCS#1 form still accepts.
steps.notes: Captured separately because the two bounds are different numbers, and a port that applied one bound to both paddings would pass a single-case check. The accepted PKCS#1 call at the identical length is what turns that from an assertion into evidence.

calls.name: acceptedUnderPkcs1
calls.notes: The SAME 87-byte payload under PKCS#1, which accepts it. This is what makes the OAEP refusal a bound rather than a general size limit.

record.bound: at most modulus minus 42 bytes, which is 86
record.pkcs1BoundAtTheSameLength: accepted, because the PKCS#1 bound is 117

steps.observes: A signature under the weakest digest identifier in the hash set, and its verification.
steps.notes: This case exists because the declaring comment names the hash set's consumers as the hash operation AND the signing and verification operations, so the whole set is a legal signature-hash selector. derive.name: observedClasses
derive.observes: Which character classes the generator actually draws from, as the union across every sample, plus the per-sample figures the union is built from. A generator that silently dropped the symbol class would produce perfectly plausible strings and would be caught only here.

record.comparisonBasis: the UNION of classes across the samples, not the classes of any one of them. Measured, not assumed: two runs of a single 24-character sample under these same flags disagreed on whether a digit was present, because the presence of a class in one short sample is a property of the sample rather than of the generator. A class absent from the alphabet can never be observed, so the union only ever gains classes that are genuinely there.
